chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Sa'dan, from Husayn ibn Ameen, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who is stingy in helping his Muslim brother and in standing for him regarding his need, will be tried with helping one who sins on his behalf and will not be recompensed.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of not helping a Muslim brother in need?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a spiritual economy where the quality of one's charity is measured by the worthiness of the recipient, warning that withholding help from a righteous brother results in being burdened with the assistance of the sinful. This reflects the Shia emphasis on 'wala' (loyalty) and 'bara' (disassociation), suggesting that neglecting communal bonds not only loses reward but incurs a specific spiritual penalty by aligning one with the unworthy. The narrative underscores the practical implication that charitable acts are transactional in a metaphysical sense, directly impacting the donor's spiritual standing.
